post.caption:
Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and still transmits from over 24 billion km away, with the signal taking around 22 hours to arrive. It was made possible by a planetary alignment that recurs roughly every 175 years, and by gravity assists: swing close to a planet and its motion flings you onward while the planet slows immeasurably. Its plutonium power source has been fading since launch, so instruments are switched off one at a time. It also turned around once and photographed Earth as less than a pixel.
